carriedFindings.XR4-3: carried (NOTE): 'No other reader role could either' holds for reading another role's image, but it misses the obvious route for the carried P1 captures: self-capture. A process can always read its own exe link, and a second process in the same domain passes both the uid rule and the capability rule. So the broker, a low-port server and the worker can each capture their own image. Naming this route would help the native-profile successor that receives the carry.
carriedFindings.XR4-4:
carried (NOTE): Two points on how the owner decision is recorded; neither changes the data.
(1) Scope. The owner's words 'The server and broker lose the reads they have no duty for' are applied to the three writer and gate pairs. The README should say so explicitly. In v4 the server's and broker's remaining /proc reads (of the observer, containment, the worker, the backend components and Pods) were also justified as reader-role captures. P1 and P5 now go to the observer, while backend captures are still unassigned. If the owner meant the decision more broadly, those reads need the same treatment, through a further question.
(2) Provenance. README:81 says the owner chose (b) 'after seeing the analysis above'. That analysis now includes the capability limit added after XR3-2: the observer cannot capture the broker's image, a low-port server's or the worker's. If the owner decided before that paragraph existed, write 'after seeing the options analysis', and have the monitor confirm the owner knows that P1's broker capture is carried. The narrowing itself stays sound, because no reader can capture these images whichever role is designated.

ownerDecisions.decision: Binding facts for slot 240: (1) credential types already published: selinux-matrix-v2's README (:112) names the gate's credential types planeon_gate_effect_cred_t and planeon_gate_writer_cred_t, the two upstream client credentials. (2) The I04 server credential (the KUBERNETES_API_PROXY endpoint's key and certificate chain, resolved spec §4.2 :288) has no named type. That's the gap 240 closes: either a new dedicated type or filing it under planeon_gate_effect_cred_t. That's your contract choice; bring it to me as an owner question if it's a real trade-off. (3) The owner decided (Q-HE3D-5 (a)) that the gate's signed configuration lives at fixed paths /etc/planeon/effect-gate/config.json and config.json.sig. The design treats that directory as labelled planeon_etc_t, writable only by planeon_maint_t in maintenance mode. The configuration names the credential and CA files with sha256 pins. No exact credential file names are fixed yet: HE-008 fixes the paths, and 240 fixes the types and access. (4) Q-HE3D-7 (d): the config-signer public key is compiled into the binary, so no key file needs a type.

F-I04-1: I04 is mutual TLS 1.3. The gate reads three things, all DER: its serving private key (PKCS#8), its serving certificate chain, and exactly ONE client CA (owner Q-HE3D-8 (a)). How the SERVER, as I04 client, holds the trust anchor for the gate and its own client credential isn't fixed in any W03 design; it's the server's side. Treat the server as reading the gate's cert/anchor only if a published contract says so. Paths, owner and mode aren't fixed yet; HE-008 fixes them. The signed configuration names the files with sha256 pins. F-I04-2: HE-008 isn't designed yet and expects no type names, so your names planeon_gate_i04_key_t / planeon_gate_i04_cert_t are fine. Add a third, CA-type decision, or fold the client CA under the cert type, in your shape. F-CAP-1: no published contract and no W03 design assigns which reader role performs the native profile's P1 role captures or the P5 lifecycle capture. It is unassigned. Decisions, monitor (owner-delegated), 2026-10-15: Q-MX-1 = (a): separate credential types, gate-only READ on the key and least privilege elsewhere; the key type joins A09. Finalise the shape, including the client CA, under F-I04-1. Q-MX-4 = (a): drop net_bind_service from the gate and from A48's allow list (owner Q-HE2S-9 (a), HS43 H5), plus the new mutation. Q-MX-5 = (a): as you specified (gate READ on planeon_cgroup_worker_t, dir search on its two parents, procAccess gate→planeon_worker_t, per-type A38/A39, A59 update). Q-MX-2 and Q-MX-3: re-frame for the owner.

Owner decisions for slot 240, 2026-10-15. Record verbatim, including that the owner first chose "keep and record" from the earlier framing and then, after seeing your analysis, chose your recommendation: Q-MX-2 = (b) and Q-MX-3 = (b). The OBSERVER is designated as the role that takes the native profile's P1 role captures and P5 lifecycle capture. That designation is carried to the next native-profile successor (primary's O-NATIVE-GATE-NOCAP packet) and to W03. The writer's /proc narrows to {gate, observer}. The gate's /proc narrows to {broker, observer}. The server and broker lose the reads they have no duty for, with A59 per-target pins plus mutations. Q-MX-1: your two-type shape is accepted: planeon_gate_i04_key_t (joins A09), and planeon_gate_i04_cert_t for the chain plus the one client CA, both gate-only READ and maintenance-only write. Q-MX-4 (a) and Q-MX-5 (a): as decided earlier.
